title: Drawing pedigrees
text: pedigree data frame one row per animal: id, sire, dam sex, generation number gen findGeneration() gives (vignette("pedkindraw") describes columns). B parents C, D E, C F parents G H. generation row: B top, offspring C, D E , G H bottom. F parents pedigree, founder like B, drawn beside mate C, row. mating small dot two mates, lines offspring, drawn right angles kinship2 draws . mating sire drawn left dam, C, D E drawn left right order rows. layout list. nodes data frame row animal mating dot, invisible points lines turn , node’s place: x, y, grows downward. ids dots points start two underscores. edges data frame row line.
code: library(pedkindraw)  fam <- data.frame(   id   = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"),   sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "A", NA, "C", "C"),   dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", "B", NA, "F", "F"),   sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "F", "F", "F", "M") ) fam$gen <- findGeneration(fam$id, fam$sire, fam$dam) layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam) drawPedigreeDiagram(layout) names(layout) #> [1] "nodes"              "edges"              "duplicateToReal"    #> [4] "isolatedIds"        "conditions"         "conditionsNotDrawn" #> [7] "hints" animals <- layout$nodes[!startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__"), ] data.frame(id = animals$id, shape = animals$shape,            x = round(animals$x), y = animals$y) #>   id  shape    x   y #> 1  A square  -10   0 #> 2  B    dot  110   0 #> 3  C square -150 150 #> 4  D    dot   90 150 #> 5  E    dot  210 150 #> 6  F    dot  -30 150 #> 7  G    dot -150 300 #> 8  H square  -30 300

title: Drawing pedigrees
text: symbol shows sex: square "M", circle "F", star "H" (hermaphrodite), triangle "U" (unknown) diamond code none (NA), “/ Unrecorded” legend. optional status column marks slash animal whose status "DECEASED". S1 D1 one offspring sex code, S1 died. legend right every drawing lists five symbols, “Affected” (see Conditions, ) “Deceased”, lines: dashed line joins two places animal, three twin lines. Hover animal see id, sex, generation, sire dam, condition; hover mating dot see many offspring . hover, animals lines near one pointer turn grey.

title: Drawing pedigrees
text: column whose name starts affected condition. one column, animal whose value TRUE (1) filled pink, FALSE (0) leaves white, NA fills grey, animal whose status known look unaffected; legend grey row “Affected status unknown”. Hovering animal says Yes, Unknown. D G affected, whether H affected known. two four condition columns, symbol cut one section per condition, filled condition’s colour animal affected, condition’s row legend shows sections filled; section whose status known grey. sections go counter-clockwise top, order columns. column’s name gives label: affected_diabetes becomes “Affected (diabetes)”. drawing grows 45 pixels taller condition past first, “Affected status unknown” row, make room legend. C diabetes, B E obese, arthritis; G diabetes obese, whether H obese known, H’s obesity section grey. fifth condition column drawn: layout names conditionsNotDrawn.

text: checkPedigree() lists problem finds, one row per problem, changes nothing. finds none example. checkTwinRelations() stops twin pair possible, instance MZ DZ twins share sire dam, otherwise returns table. Records problems look like . s2 sire o2 row , d1, dam o1 o2, recorded male. addParents() adds row sire dam none, marks rows recordStatus column. correctParentSex() sets sex sire recorded female dam recorded male. , check finds nothing.

title: Getting started with pedkindraw
text: kinship() computes kinship coefficient every pair animals: chance allele taken random one animal allele taken random identical descent. animal’s coefficient 0.5, inbred. sparse = TRUE returns sparse matrix, saves memory large pedigree. E06FRB HV7LZ3 identical (MZ) twins. twins table gives coefficient 0.5, ; without 0.25, full siblings. 8GSXTQ P844CW fraternal (DZ) twins, full siblings, 0.25. animal whose sire dam related inbred. example 29 animals. One ED5PDV. sire 81MJXH dam H16XSK half siblings, offspring YPHFHF, kinship coefficient 0.125. ED5PDV’s coefficient (1 + 0.125) / 2 = 0.5625.
code: k <- kinship(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam, ped$gen, twinRelations = twins) dim(k) #> [1] 375 375 k[c("E06FRB", "HV7LZ3", "8GSXTQ", "P844CW"),   c("E06FRB", "HV7LZ3", "8GSXTQ", "P844CW")] #>        E06FRB HV7LZ3 8GSXTQ P844CW #> E06FRB    0.5    0.5   0.00   0.00 #> HV7LZ3    0.5    0.5   0.00   0.00 #> 8GSXTQ    0.0    0.0   0.50   0.25 #> P844CW    0.0    0.0   0.25   0.50 sum(diag(k) > 0.5) #> [1] 29 k[c("81MJXH", "H16XSK", "ED5PDV"), c("81MJXH", "H16XSK", "ED5PDV")] #>        81MJXH H16XSK ED5PDV #> 81MJXH 0.5000 0.1250 0.3125 #> H16XSK 0.1250 0.5000 0.3125 #> ED5PDV 0.3125 0.3125 0.5625

title: Getting started with pedkindraw
text: shrinkPedigree() trims pedigree animals needed keep informative within budget bit size, given animals genotyped , optionally, affected. follows kinship2’s pedigree.shrink(). bit size, bitSize() gives, twice number animals known parent less number founders. example genotypes, 30 percent animals picked random stand genotyped ones: 109 375. whole pedigree’s bit size 2 * 251 - 124 = 378. works steps. first removes 104 unavailable animals: genotyped left offspring, founders add nothing. removes 4 genotyped animals offspring left whose sire dam genotyped. takes pedigree 375 animals 267, bit size 378 237. Last, removes one genotyped animal offspring left time, time one whose removal leaves smallest bit size, animals removal leaves unavailable, bit size 16. takes 214 animals leaves 53, bit size 16. help page gives rule.
code: set.seed(42) genotyped <- runif(nrow(ped)) < 0.3 sum(genotyped) #> [1] 109 bitSize(ped) #> $bitSize #> [1] 378 #>  #> $nFounder #> [1] 124 #>  #> $nNonFounder #> [1] 251 shrunk <- shrinkPedigree(ped, genotyped, maxBits = 16L) lengths(shrunk$idList) #>   unavail noninform  affected  #>       104         4       214 c(shrunk$pedSizeOriginal, shrunk$pedSizeIntermed, shrunk$pedSizeFinal) #> [1] 375 267  53 shrunk$bitSize[c(1L, 2L, length(shrunk$bitSize))] #> [1] 378 237  16

what: Shrink a pedigree to fit within a bit-size budget — shrinkPedigree
title: Shrink a pedigree to fit within a bit-size budget — shrinkPedigree
text: Trims pedigree individuals needed keep genetically informative within genotyping-cost budget (maxBits), given individuals genotyped (genotyped) , optionally, affected trait interest (affected). follows method kinship2::pedigree.shrink(), working package's id/sire/dam data-frame pedigree. Three tiers applied order: Unavailable trim. Iteratively removes terminal (leaf) individuals genotyped, removes founder couple exactly one child together mate, parents founders neither genotyped (couple's shared child promoted founder status rather removed), removes remaining childless founder ("stray marry-") regardless genotyped status. Non-informative trim. Removes genotyped, non-parent individual whose sire dam known genotyped, individual affected (NA affected status counts unaffected ) – add genotype information beyond parents already supply. individual one known parent (one sire/dam known, NA) never trimmed tier. partial parentage ordinary data package (see getIdsWithOneParent), whereas kinship2 allow . Affected-priority trim. pedigree's bit size (2 * nNonFounder - nFounder) still exceeds maxBits, removes one genotyped, non-parent individual time – trying NA-affected candidates first, unaffected, affected – choosing whichever single candidate's removal (including cascade tiers 1-2 ) minimizes resulting bit size. Ties go first id byte order (capitals lower case, sort(method = "radix") orders text), whatever computer's language setting, input always gives answer (kinship2 breaks ties random). idTrimmed idList$affected record every id actually removed round, including removed cascade, pedSizeOriginal - pedSizeFinal always equals length(idTrimmed).

title: Shrink a pedigree to fit within a bit-size budget — shrinkPedigree
code: ## Seven animals: C and D are full siblings, and so are F and G, D's ## offspring ped <- data.frame(   id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G"),   sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "D", "D"),   dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E", "E"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) genotyped <- rep(TRUE, nrow(ped)) result <- shrinkPedigree(ped, genotyped, maxBits = 16L) nrow(ped) #> [1] 7 ## With every individual genotyped, the whole pedigree can be trimmed away. nrow(result$ped) #> [1] 0  ## Only F and G genotyped: C, not genotyped and with no offspring, is ## removed, and then A and B, founders left with one offspring, D, who ## becomes a founder. result <- shrinkPedigree(ped, genotyped = ped$id %in% c("F", "G")) result$ped$id #> [1] "D" "E" "F" "G" result$idTrimmed #> [1] "C" "A" "B"  ## To see what shrinking removed, draw the whole pedigree with the removed ## animals filled. A column whose name starts with "affected" is drawn as a ## condition; the legend and the hover text call this one ## "Affected (removed)". ped$sex <- c("M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "F") ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam) ped$affected_removed <- ped$id %in% result$idTrimmed layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped) diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout) ## Print `diagram` in an interactive session to see it.
